title: Toy Story 5 Breaks a Billion-Dollar Record — Three Times in a Row!
summary: Imagine your favorite toys coming to life — again! Toy Story 5 just did something no other cartoon movie series has ever done. It zoomed past $1 billion at the global box office. That's a one with nine zeros! But here's the really cool part: it's the third Toy Story movie in a row to hit that giant number. Toy Story 3 and Toy Story 4 both made over $1 billion too. No other animated franchise has ever done that. Not Minions, not Shrek, not even Frozen — yet. So what's the new movie about? Woody, Buzz, Jessie, and the whole gang meet a new gadget: a tablet named Lilypad. She has big ideas about how to play with Bonnie, their kid. The toys worry they might get replaced. It's a funny, heartwarming adventure that fans and critics loved. The movie is now the top-earning film of 2026, just ahead of The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. But watch out — a big new movie called The Odyssey is catching up fast. Still, for now, Pixar gets to wear the crown. This is a huge win for Pixar. Lately, some of their movies didn't make as much money in theaters. But hits like Inside Out 2 and now Toy Story 5 are helping them keep making awesome original stories. So if you haven't seen it yet, grab some popcorn and head to the theater. You'll laugh, you might tear up a little, and you'll see why these toys are still stars after 30 years.
why_it_matters: Just like you might have a favorite toy that feels like a real friend, this story shows how toys can stay exciting and make us laugh for generations.

background_read: Pixar Animation Studios—the company behind Toy Story, Finding Nemo, and Inside Out—made the first full computer-animated movie in 1995 with the original Toy Story.
Movies earn money by selling tickets at theaters all over the world. When a film passes $1 billion in ticket sales, it is called a box-office hit.
Sequels like Toy Story 5 help studios pay for brand-new, original movies because big hits bring in money that can be used for risky ideas.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Toy Story characters (Woody, Buzz, Jessie) and a new gadget named Lilypad.
WHAT: Toy Story 5 earned more than $1 billion worldwide, making it the third movie in the Toy Story franchise to reach that mark in a row.
WHERE: At the global box office—movie theaters in many different countries.
WHY: Fans and critics loved the funny, heartwarming adventure, and it helped Pixar recover after some other movies did not perform as well.

perspectives.description: Fans are thrilled to see their favorite characters return and are happy that the toys are still popular after all these years.
Some people might think making too many sequels means there are fewer chances for completely new and different movies.
Movie studios need big hits like Toy Story 5 to earn enough money, so they can later take risks on fresh, original stories that might not be huge successes at first.
